newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Maystadt - Stability pact needs ministerial overview.
newsitem.headline: Maystadt - Stability pact needs ministerial overview.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Thursday there had been a fairly favourable response to his country's proposal for a compromise on a pact to ensure fiscal discipline under the EU's planned monetary union.
"The response was fairly favourable," he told a news briefing. He declined to say exactly what the Belgian compromise was, but said it was based on the Maastricht treaty.
"We have a basis which is the treaty. There is nothing about automaticity. It is the Council (ministers) which can decide on the basis of a global assessment," he said.
He confirmed that Belgium had indeed put forward compromise proposals. "I believe it is a bit of a tradition for Belgium to seek a compromise," he said.

He was speaking during a pause in talks between EU ministers aimed at resolving a dispute over the budget stability pact which is meant to ensure countries maintain fiscal discipline after the launch of the single currency in 1999.
Maystadt said ministers were 95 percent agreed on the stability pact, but still had to work out how to define the exceptional circumstances which would exempt countries from fines under the pact.
The ministerial talks, taking place on the eve of a summit of EU leaders, were likely to drag on for some time.
But he said EU leaders would prefer the dispute on the stability pact to be settled by finance ministers rather than allowing the discussions to drag on into the summit.
"In my opinion the heads of state would prefer for it to be agreed between us," he said.
He said there were several delegations in favour of a fairly strict definition of the kind of exceptional circumstances which would justify an exemption from fines.
There were several options on the table in defining these exceptional circumstances, he said.
